services.heroParagraphs: Ivy Cleans is a local, insured business, and we handle residential cleaning and janitorial work in homes and offices throughout Orlando. Our team has done this long enough to know where the dirt hides here: the fan blades that never stop turning, the sliding door track that fills with sand, the return vent above the hallway, the top edge of the shower door. You get professional house cleaners who arrive ready to work, bring their own products and equipment, and leave rooms that smell like nothing at all rather than like a bottle of cleaner.

We’re happy to have you check behind us. Run a finger along a baseboard, open the shower door, look under the dining chairs. A one-bedroom condo downtown and a five-bedroom house with a pool cage get the same standard of work from our team. We also tell you the truth about what came out and what didn’t, because etched hard water spots and years-old grout staining take repeat visits, not promises.
Is mildew creeping back into your shower grout? When did your ceiling fan blades last get wiped? Who’s handling the pollen that settles on the lanai furniture every spring?
Home or business, call our professional cleaning company today and ask for a quote on the work you need done.
Give Ivy Cleans a call and we’ll put together an estimate for your place.
services.serviceIntro: Ivy Cleans provides a full range of professional cleaning services in Orlando and the surrounding towns, from regular maid service and deep cleaning in houses, condos and rentals to office upkeep and janitorial work for local businesses. Our house cleaners are experienced, and they work with quality products and equipment chosen for tile, terrazzo, granite, stucco sills and everything else common in Central Florida homes. Schedules here rarely sit still, so we build cleaning visits around yours, weekly, every other week or monthly.

Live oaks let go of pollen from February onward, and it drifts through screens, doors and open garages until every flat surface wears a yellow film. The air handler runs most of the year and moves that fine grit around indoors. Our dusting service takes it off blinds, shelves, fan blades and vents.

Sand comes in on flip-flops from yards, ball fields and parking lots, and a long afternoon at a theme park sends grit and sunscreen straight onto the floor at the end of the day. Our vacuuming reaches carpet, area rugs, tile grout lines and the edges along baseboards where it collects.

Summer humidity sits inside a bathroom long after the shower is off, and Central Florida’s mineral-heavy water leaves chalky rings on fixtures and glass. We scrub grout, caulk lines, tile and toilets, cut through the film on shower doors, and clear out the germs so the room stays a safe, healthy space for your family.

Pollen film, sprinkler overspray, and afternoon thunderstorms that dry into spotted glass keep Orlando windows cloudy, and love bug season finishes the job. Our window cleaners wash the glass, wipe the tracks and frames, and get the sliders clear again so your rooms take in the light they were built for.
sections.services.cards.dusting: Dusting matters here because the ceiling fans barely stop turning and the air conditioning circulates fine particles through the house all year. Add spring pollen and the dust kicked up by nearby construction, and surfaces go gritty within days. Our team wipes blinds, plantation shutters, fan blades, baseboards, light fixtures and shelves, so the air in your rooms feels cleaner and the furniture stays looking cared for.
sections.services.cards.vacuuming: Vacuuming keeps ahead of the sandy soil that Orlando households track in from driveways, playgrounds and pool decks, along with pet hair that clings in a humid house. Carpet holds it, tile pushes it into the grout, and rugs by the back door take the worst of it. We vacuum thoroughly, edges and under furniture included, and leave floors that feel clean underfoot.
sections.services.cards.bathroom: Bathrooms work hard in this climate. Warm, damp air lingers after every shower, mildew finds the caulk and grout, and hard water leaves a stubborn haze on glass and chrome. Our cleaners scour tile, tubs, sinks, toilets and shower doors, disinfect the surfaces hands touch most, and wipe down the exhaust vent, leaving a bathroom that stays fresher between visits.
sections.services.cards.window: Windows in Orlando take a beating from sprinkler spray, storm-driven grime, pollen and the bugs that show up twice a year in clouds. Big sliders and lanai glass show every bit of it once the afternoon sun hits. We wash the panes inside and out where we can reach safely, clean the sills and tracks, and give your rooms back their view.
sections.services.cards.upholstery: Sofas and armchairs absorb what Orlando living puts on them: sunscreen, chlorine off damp pool towels, pet hair, pollen that settles into the cushions, and the musty edge humidity gives fabric that sits in a closed-up house. Our upholstery cleaning lifts the soil out of the weave, treats spots, and knocks down odors, so the furniture your family actually uses feels fresh again.
sections.suburb.winter-park.intro: We clean houses across Winter Park, from the mid-century ranch streets to the estates sitting on the chain of lakes. The live oak canopy shows up in the work before anything else does: acorns, leaf fall and fine bark dust settle on porches, mats and lanai tile all year, and every bit of it walks into the entry hall on shoes. We quote entry and lanai work here as its own piece of the job rather than assuming it, because in most homes on these brick streets it genuinely is.
sections.suburb.winter-park.homes: Two very different jobs share one area name here. The century-old brick estates near Park Avenue have original millwork, deep baseboards, detailed trim and old tile and fixtures, so a deep clean on one of the older estates is hand-work and hours, not speed. Windsong, built between 2001 and 2016, runs from around 2,755 to 5,196 square feet — open kitchens, tall glass, long runs of hard flooring a crew can cover fast. Windsong Estates adds larger lakeside footprints and more bathrooms per house. At Winter Park Pines Condominiums the scale flips again, with compact rooms and older fittings, and regular upkeep in a Winter Park Pines condo is a different visit entirely. We estimate by house, never by street average.
sections.suburb.winter-park.local: Organic litter off the oaks never really stops, and the grit that comes off the brick roads rides in with it, so a standard clean here starts at the doors and mats before anything else. On the lakefront and canal-side houses, the rear entry takes the beating instead — wet feet from the dock, sand, lake grass, dog paws and towels tracked across tile and back through the family room. Add Central Florida’s humidity, which keeps bathroom grout and closet corners damp enough to grow mildew, air conditioning that pushes dust into every vent and blind, and spring pollen coating sills and window tracks, and there’s a clear order to the work in these homes.
sections.suburb.maitland.intro: We clean houses in Maitland every week, and the glass is what sets the work apart here. Mid-century homes on these streets were built with wide single-pane windows and sliders, so interior sills, tracks and frames take up more of our time than the square footage would suggest. Add lake-access lots off the Winter Park Chain of Lakes, and rear doors see wet feet and sand year round. We plan the visit around both.
sections.suburb.maitland.homes: Dommerich Estates started going up in 1957 and never really stopped, which is why one street can hold a 1,422 square foot ranch and a 5,178 square foot custom house a few doors down; one listing there credits a 1961 Paul Pizer design. Dommerich Hills and Indian Hills run the same way. Some kitchens and bathrooms are still original, with tile and grout old enough that we plan deep cleaning of aged tile and grout rather than a quick pass. Others have been taken back to the studs and rebuilt, with stone counters and frameless glass showers that want a lighter hand and different products. Rooms in the bigger houses open into each other, so floors get done in long runs instead of room by room.
sections.suburb.maitland.local: Lake days end at the back door, so the sand and damp footprints from Chain of Lakes access collect on rear entry tile and in the grout lines before they ever reach the living room, and that’s where we start. Those big panes of single-pane glass hold every fingerprint and every ring of dried spray, and the interior sills below them catch pollen in spring. Summer humidity keeps hall baths and closets damp enough for mildew to take hold along caulk and shower corners. The air conditioning runs most of the year and pushes fine dust onto blinds, ledges and ceiling fan blades, which is why keeping up with it on a regular schedule beats one big push in October.
sections.suburb.altamonte-springs.intro: We clean houses in Altamonte Springs most weeks of the year, and a lot of them are alike in the ways that matter to the work: three bedrooms, two baths, built somewhere between the early seventies and the late nineties, on streets where no HOA has an opinion about your driveway. That kind of housing stock rewards steady recurring maintenance cleans far more than twice-a-year rescues — same tile, same fixtures, same shower door, just kept on top of.
sections.suburb.altamonte-springs.homes: Spring Valley is the heart of it, medium three- and four-bedroom single-family homes, mostly owner-occupied, with apartment buildings sitting along the wider roads. Spring Valley Farms runs much the same, on lots that have absorbed thirty years of screened porches and back-room additions. Sanlando Springs leans smaller and more rental, modest houses and apartments where turnover is a regular fact of life. Almost everything here went up between 1970 and 1999, with a little newer infill scattered through. Expect tile in kitchens and baths, carpet in the bedrooms, sliding glass doors onto a patio slab, and original tub surrounds with grout older than the people using them. We clean apartments in Sanlando Springs the same week we clean houses two streets away.
sections.suburb.altamonte-springs.local: Those fifty-year-old bathrooms are the honest problem here. Aged grout, shrinking caulk and etched shower glass hold soap film and mineral haze in a way no quick wipe touches, so a restorative deep clean lifts back everything that will lift, and we’ll tell you plainly when what’s left is a re-grout job rather than dirt. Beyond that, it’s Florida doing what it does. The air conditioning runs nearly all year and keeps pushing dust onto vent registers, ceiling fan blades and the tops of door frames, summer storms track grit across tile from the carport door inward, and oak pollen in late winter settles yellow on windowsills, blinds and screened porch furniture until someone washes it off.
sections.suburb.college-park.intro: Our crews work in College Park nearly every week, and the first thing we plan around is parking. The brick streets this close to downtown are narrow, most houses have a short driveway or none at all, and we carry our gear in from the curb. That shapes how we schedule a morning. Once we’re inside, it’s old-house work: original wood floors, painted woodwork, and small rooms laid out long before anyone wanted an open plan. We clean around all of it carefully.
sections.suburb.college-park.homes: Most of what we clean here went up between the 1920s land boom and 1940. Craftsman bungalows and Mediterranean Revival cottages in the Lake Adair-Lake Concord Historic District, modest single-story homes on the streets of Rosemere and Edgewater Heights, and around the Lake Ivanhoe Historic Residential District a mix of early-1900s cottages standing next to contemporary infill. Rooms are small, and there’s far more door casing, baseboard and built-in shelving per square foot than in anything built since. Floors are usually the original pine or oak, and the bathrooms are often the ones the house was born with, small, tiled, and grouted decades before we got there. A deep clean here is measured in trim, not floor area.
sections.suburb.college-park.local: Old houses hold dust where new ones don’t — the top edge of a door casing, the bead on a picture rail, the gap behind a hundred-year-old baseboard. We vacuum and hand-wipe that millwork instead of spraying it, because original paint and finished pine won’t forgive a harsh cleaner. Homes along Dubsdread and the lakes take grass clippings and lake grit in at the back door, so we start at the rear entry and work forward. The rest is Orlando: air conditioning running most of the year and pushing dust through every register, humidity settling into a small tiled bathroom, oak pollen on sills and blinds each spring. When a bungalow is going on the market, we work through it room by room.
sections.suburb.lake-nona.intro: We clean houses across Lake Nona, from Laureate Park to Lake Nona Central. The layout drives the job here more than the square footage: most of these homes are two-story, so our cleaners spend real time on stairs, upstairs baths and the tall entry glass that shows every fingerprint. The other thing is the gates — at guard-gated entries our crew has to be registered by name ahead of the visit, not handed a code, so we sort that out when we book.
sections.suburb.lake-nona.homes: The newest housing stock in the metro sits out here — 17 square miles of it, most under twenty years old, built by Toll Brothers, ICI Homes, Dream Finders, Pulte, Beazer and David Weekley. Laureate Park gives us open downstairs plans with long runs of tile and carpet on the stairs and bedroom level. Summerdale Park is two-story new construction, where we’re mostly dealing with new construction dust settling on fresh baseboards and inside cabinets. VillageWalk at Lake Nona is guard-gated with conservation homesites and maintenance-free living, so the yard and the exterior are already someone else’s job and ours is everything inside the door. For most of these houses the work is steady upkeep, and our regular every-other-week cleaning keeps grout and stair treads from slipping.
sections.suburb.lake-nona.local: Houses on conservation homesites back onto undeveloped land, and it shows on the glass: rear sliders and lanai screens collect leaf litter, pollen and spider webbing at a rate an interior-lot house never sees, so a deep clean of sliders, screens and lanai tile is usually where we start. Two floors also means the dust lives upstairs, on loft railings, high window ledges and the second-floor baths nobody looks at twice. Then there’s the rest of Orlando: air conditioning running ten or eleven months a year and pushing dust through every vent, showers that stay damp long enough for mildew to take hold in the grout, and oak pollen that yellows sills and blinds each spring.
sections.suburb.dr-phillips.intro: We clean homes all over Dr. Phillips, from the single-story streets off Turkey Lake Road to the big houses on the Butler Chain lakefront. A good share of the addresses we visit sit behind a gate, and several of those gates are staffed, so we sort the code, the guard list and the community’s vendor rules before the day of the visit rather than at the callbox. That’s usually what stands between a recurring clean that starts on time and one that runs an hour late.
sections.suburb.dr-phillips.homes: The housing runs in three registers here. Emerald Forest and Turtle Creek are the older side: 1960s and 1970s ranches on wide lots, one story, terrazzo or tile under carpet somebody added later, original bathrooms with tile grout that needs scrubbing rather than wiping. Casa Del Lago and Phillips Bay Estates are newer and taller, with two-story foyers, wood plank floors and stacked sliders facing water, which means glass and stair rails on every visit. Then Bay Hill and Vizcaya, where the estates carry pool decks, guest suites and long runs of glass; those take a bigger crew and most of a day. When one of the older ranches changes hands, the kitchen and baths usually need a full reset first.
sections.suburb.dr-phillips.local: Houses that back onto the golf courses at Bay Hill or sit on a lake in Isle of Osprey take in grass clippings, irrigation grit and fine sand at the patio door all year. It collects in the slider tracks, along the baseboards on the pool side, and in the first three feet of every rug inside a back door, so those are the spots we work first. Sunscreen and pool spray leave a film on the glass. After that it’s the Orlando list: summer humidity that keeps guest baths and closets damp enough for mildew in the grout, air conditioning running most of the year and dropping dust on ceiling fans and blinds, and oak pollen every spring on sills and screens.
sections.suburb.windermere.intro: We clean houses in Windermere, on both sides of the town line — inside the 2.2 square miles bounded by Lake Butler, Lake Down and Lake Bessie, and out through the wider 34786 area toward Disney’s eastern boundary. Nearly every street sits behind a gate, so our team keeps insurance documentation current and registers with each community on its own terms rather than assuming one clearance covers the whole town. It’s a small place with a lot of square footage under roof.
sections.suburb.windermere.homes: The estate streets — Lake Down Cove, Keene’s Pointe, Lake Butler Sound and Waterstone on Lake Butler — run to Colonial Revival, New Traditional and Contemporary builds with two-story entries, wide stone or wood floors, and walls of glass turned toward the water. Rooms are big and there are a lot of them: guest wings, summer kitchens, pool baths and sliders opening onto docks. Fittings are often newer than the architecture suggests, so polished nickel, marble counters and frameless shower glass get the gentler products and the slower pass. In Lake Burden and the Lakes of Windermere the product changes completely — townhomes and condos with tile downstairs, carpet up, and one hall bath doing all the work. Condo and townhome cleaning here is a different job at a different scale.
sections.suburb.windermere.local: Inside the Town, WastePro wants everything at the curb by 7:00 a.m., so we sort out ahead of time whether bagged waste goes into your cans for the next pickup or leaves with our van; in unincorporated 34786 the subdivision’s hauler or Orange County sets the rules instead. Lake-facing glass is the other constant here — pool spray, dock traffic and the haze that settles on sliders turned toward Lake Down and Lake Butler. Summer humidity keeps pool baths and closets damp enough for mildew to take hold along grout, the air handlers run nearly year round and push dust onto blinds and baseboards, and oak pollen in late winter dulls every windowsill. Deep cleaning after pollen season resets those surfaces.
sections.suburb.winter-garden.intro: We clean houses across Winter Garden, from the older streets near Lake Apopka out to the newer rooftops along the 429 Expressway. Most of what we do here is recurring cleaning on a set schedule, because the neighborhoods sit close enough together that a crew can cover several houses in a day without losing the morning to driving. Fourteen miles from downtown Orlando, and the pace of the day out here is nothing like it.
sections.suburb.winter-garden.homes: Much of the housing stock is recent. Summerlake, Hamlin and Johns Lake Pointe went up as production builds with open kitchens running into the family room, tile or luxury vinyl across the first floor, and carpet upstairs. Big rooms, few walls, one continuous floor, so floors take the bulk of the visit. On a new handover we clear the construction dust off the tops of cabinets before anyone moves in. Independence is gated with its own elementary school, and its earliest phases are old enough that grout has darkened and shower glass carries hard water film. Orchard Hills and the established streets closer to downtown have smaller, separate rooms and older fittings that take longer per square foot; those usually start with a deep clean of grout and glass.
sections.suburb.winter-garden.local: Independence and Orchard Hills fill up with young families, so the real work is floors, door handles, light switches and bathrooms — detail dusting matters far less than the surfaces a four-year-old touches forty times a day. Gated entries mean checking in first, though staff on the gates around the clock keeps that simple for our crews. The rest of it is Orlando. Air conditioning runs ten or eleven months of the year and drives fine dust onto blinds and fan blades. Summer humidity keeps shower corners and closet walls damp enough for mildew to take hold, so we scrub the grout lines and dry the glass rather than just wiping it. Sand and clipped grass ride in from the yards and settle along baseboards and in tile grout.
sections.suburb.ocoee.intro: We clean houses all over Ocoee, and the thing that shapes our schedule here isn’t drive time, it’s the gate. Nearly every neighborhood sits behind a mandatory HOA and a call box, so we settle access codes or guest-list entry before the first visit instead of idling at the entrance. After that it’s ordinary good work: recurring cleaning for homes that mostly run 1,600 to 2,300 square feet, and move-out cleans when one changes hands.
sections.suburb.ocoee.homes: Wesmere went up mostly between 1991 and the early 2000s — Calton, Beazer and Arvida homes wrapped around fountain ponds across sixteen cul-de-sacs, close to a hundred of them waterfront. Forestbrooke followed from 2003 to 2012, Meritage and D.R. Horton. Forest Lake Estates is newer still, 278 homesites built 2017 to 2020, ranging from 1,532 to 4,182 square feet. That spread shows up in a single day’s route. A Wesmere kitchen means original grout, older glass shower doors and a deep clean that runs longer than the square footage suggests; a Forest Lake Estates great room means vinyl plank and lighter upkeep. Townhomes near Plantation Grove hold about 1,653 square feet over two floors, so most of the work is stairs and bathrooms.
sections.suburb.ocoee.local: Sprinkler heads along the pond banks in Wesmere and Westyn Bay throw hard water at the back of the house every morning, and it dries as a white film on sliders, lanai screens and the low windows off the family room, so rear glass gets its own pass on every visit. Water-adjacent living means the back door is the busy door here — grass clippings, pollen and lake grit come in that way, not the front. Add the rest of it: summer humidity that keeps guest baths and linen closets damp enough for mildew, air conditioning that runs almost all year and drifts dust onto blinds and ceiling fans, and the yellow oak pollen that coats sills each spring.
sections.suburb.apopka.intro: We clean houses all over Apopka, from the small ranch streets off the old downtown grid to the newer estate pods out toward Kelly Park Road. Distance is the first thing you notice working here. With well over a hundred subdivisions spread across town and driveways long enough to add real minutes at every stop, we build our routes tight and keep our regular housekeeping visits on a steady day and time so nobody sits waiting on a crew that’s stuck three neighborhoods away.
sections.suburb.apopka.homes: Head toward the old downtown grid and you get 1950s and 1960s ranches — single storey, compact rooms, terrazzo or original tile, bathrooms wearing the fixtures they were built with. Those usually want a deep clean of tile grout and old fixtures before any routine schedule makes sense, and they’re often where we’re doing move-out cleaning before a sale. Errol Estates and its pockets, Parkside and Linkside Village and Magnolia Woods, are golf-course homes with sunken living areas and a lot of glass to keep clear. Rock Springs Ridge, Oak Hill Reserve and Maudehelen run newer and mostly two-story, with tall entry walls, wide tile downstairs and carpet up, on lots bigger than most of Central Florida still builds.
sections.suburb.apopka.local: Cypress and oak litter is the constant here. Houses on the shaded lake lots and the ones backing state-park land — Rock Springs Estates especially, with woods on nearly every side — collect leaf fall, bark and seed against door tracks, screen panels and lanai floors, and all of it walks in on shoes. We work those entry zones on every visit instead of treating them as an extra. Inside, the air conditioning runs nearly year round and keeps a fine gray dust settling on blinds, fan blades and baseboards, summer humidity puts mildew in shower corners and closet walls, and spring pollen films the windowsills on whatever side of the house faces the yard.
sections.service.standard-cleaning.local: Humidity is what moves a standard clean around here. Bathrooms wiped down two weeks ago still show a gray film along the caulk line and the shower track, so that’s where our team starts rather than finishes, and we dry surfaces down instead of leaving them damp. Ceiling fans run twelve months a year, so the blades load up far faster than they would somewhere with a real winter, and we wipe them every visit rather than now and then. Then there’s the oak pollen. From late February that yellow-green dust is back on tile floors and window sills within a day, and in the older bungalows in College Park with original windows it gets inside no matter what, so we work floors last.
sections.service.deep-cleaning.local: Humidity is what makes a deep clean here different work. With the AC running most of the year, moisture settles where nobody looks: shower grout and caulk lines, window tracks, the channel under the sliders out to the lanai, and the return vent grilles. Those surfaces we scrub and then dry rather than just wipe, because mildew comes back on anything left damp. Spring is the other thing. The live oaks drop pollen in sheets over College Park and Winter Park, and it drifts past screens onto baseboards, fan blades, and the tops of door frames — exactly the ledges a weekly tidy skips. We work top down through the house so that layer leaves with us instead of resettling on the floors we just did.
sections.service.apartment-cleaning.local: Apartment air here runs cold and damp most of the year, and that changes what we spend our time on. Interior bathrooms with a vent fan and no window hold shower steam for hours, so we work the grout above the tub and the ceiling corners before mildew takes hold, and we wipe the AC vents and the closet wall behind them where condensation quietly settles. The other thing is the slider. Nearly every unit has a balcony or lanai, and the track collects pollen, dust, and lovebugs until the door drags, so we scrape and vacuum it out rather than run a cloth over the glass. In the newer buildings around Lake Nona that means a lot of tall glass; in older walk-ups in College Park it means painted-shut windows and deeper sills.
sections.service.airbnb-cleaning.local: Most of the rentals we turn here are built for park crowds — eight and twelve-sleeper pool homes in Windermere and Dr. Phillips where four families share bunk rooms, a game room and a screened lanai. Checkout leaves us sunscreen on the pool deck, wet towels on every rail, popcorn under the sectional and a fridge of half-drunk juice, and the whole house has to be reset before the next check-in that same afternoon. Humidity is the other half of the job. With the AC held low and the slider opening all day, we dry shower surrounds and door tracks instead of just wiping them, run the bath fans, and put nothing damp in a closet where it’ll smell by the weekend.
sections.service.post-construction-cleaning.local: Drywall dust behaves differently in this humidity. It doesn’t stay a powder — it pulls moisture overnight and sets into a gray film that a dry cloth polishes instead of lifting, so we work wet, change our water often, and go back over glass, sills and baseboards a second time after the room has sat. If the air handler ran during the work, dust is in the ductwork too, and it keeps falling for weeks unless the registers, returns and grilles are cleaned along with everything else. Older additions in College Park and Winter Park bring plaster grit and terrazzo that take different handling than the porcelain tile and painted trim in a new Lake Nona build, so we sort out what we’re dealing with before the first bucket comes in.
sections.service.pre-listing-cleaning.local: A vacant house here with the AC dialed back grows a smell before it grows anything else. Two weeks of August humidity and you’ve got mildew spotting in the shower grout, film on the window glass, and dust in the return vents that shows up in every listing photo. So on empty homes we run the air while we work, wipe the vents and the sills, and take the bathrooms down to the grout instead of just wiping surfaces — buyers notice odor before they notice anything you’ve staged. After that it’s the house itself. The 1920s bungalows in College Park hold dust in floorboard gaps and painted-over window casings, while a new build near Lake Nona is mostly construction dust on fan blades and inside the cabinets.

Let me start with the areas and neighborhoods around Orlando.Now let me research subdivisions in the western and southern suburbs.Now the northern suburbs and in-city neighborhoods.Now Lake Nona subdivisions plus adjacency checks.## Important limitation, stated up front

My web-search budget was exhausted partway through this brief. Everything below comes from pages I actually retrieved, attributed to the source. Two requested items I did **not** get to research and therefore report **nothing** on, rather than reconstruct from memory:

- **(c) part 1 — Orlando-wide climate, housing stock age, flooring/foundation type, and dirt drivers** (humidity/mold, pollen, hard water, year-round A/C, etc.). Not retrieved. Do not write this section from this brief.
- **(d) KEYWORDS.** Not retrieved. I have zero search evidence for what Orlando residents type, so I am supplying none.

These two are the top priorities for a second pass.

---

# (a) AREAS

Twelve places, all municipalities or recognised neighborhoods (no housing developments promoted to peer status).

| # | Area (local spelling) | Position relative to Orlando | Source basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Winter Park** | Just north of downtown Orlando | 407apartments: "Located just north of downtown Orlando"; Landing describes it as a cultural hub north of Orlando |
| 2 | **Maitland** | North of Winter Park | Nextdoor places Maitland's Dommerich Estates "north-west of Winter Park" |
| 3 | **Altamonte Springs** | ~10 miles north of Orlando, Seminole County | Homes.com: "a mid-sized city about 10 miles north of Orlando" |
| 4 | **Baldwin Park** | Orlando city neighborhood, NE of downtown | Wikipedia list of Orlando neighborhoods (annexed 1947, former Naval Training Center); Homes.com |
| 5 | **College Park** | Orlando city neighborhood, NW of downtown, <2 mi from downtown | Trulia: "located northwest of downtown"; Homes.com: "less than 2 miles" |
| 6 | **Lake Nona** | SE Orlando, next to Orlando International Airport | Jome/Tavistock: 17-square-mile community "Next door to the Orlando International Airport" |
| 7 | **Hunter's Creek** | South Orange County, ZIP 32837, east of Disney/US-192 corridor | Wikipedia (CDP, pop. 24,433 in 2020); MaxLife Realty |
| 8 | **Dr. Phillips** | Southwest, unincorporated Orange County, between Universal and Bay Hill | Market Connect Realty |
| 9 | **Windermere** | ~14 miles west of downtown, SW Orange County on the Butler Chain | Florida Neighborhood Realty |
| 10 | **Winter Garden** | ~14 miles west of downtown, on Lake Apopka | Nicole Mickle guide |
| 11 | **Ocoee** | West, ~11 miles from downtown (per a Forest Lake Estates listing page) | Realty in Orlando |
| 12 | **Apopka** | Northwest, near Wekiwa Springs State Park | Nextdoor / Market Connect Realty |

## Adjacency — separated by what the pages actually said

**Confirmed on a retrieved page:**
- **Baldwin Park ↔ Winter Park** — the West Orange Times & Observer piece on Baldwin Park describes roads reconnected to "create a seamless interface between adjacent neighborhoods of Orlando and Winter Park," specifically Lakemont continuing past Lake Baldwin.
- **Windermere ↔ Dr. Phillips** — Florida Neighborhood Realty: Dr. Phillips is "immediately east" of Windermere's 34786 area.
- **Ocoee ↔ Windermere** — Florida Neighborhood Realty: "Wesmere sits in south Ocoee just north of the Windermere line."
- **Ocoee ↔ Apopka** — the Forestbrooke page places it in north Ocoee off Ocoee-Apopka Road, bordered by Apopka homes.
- **Maitland ↔ Winter Park** — Nextdoor's Dommerich Estates page positions that Maitland neighborhood immediately north-west of Winter Park.
- **Winter Garden ↔ Windermere** (weaker, but sourced) — Nextdoor places Winter Garden's Independence "south-west of Summerport," and Summerport is repeatedly listed as a Windermere-area (34786) subdivision.

# (c) HOUSING AND LOCAL CONDITIONS

## Orlando as a whole

**Not researched — nothing reported.** I did not retrieve a single page on Orlando's climate, seasons, soil, foundation type, flooring conventions, humidity/mold, pollen, or water hardness. Anything I wrote here would be exactly the plausible reconstruction you told me to avoid. This is the first thing to search next: Orlando climate normals, Florida slab-on-grade construction and tile flooring conventions, Orange County water hardness, Central Florida pollen calendar.

## Area by area

Format: **sourced fact** → *what it means for cleaning (my inference from that fact, not a sourced claim).*

**Winter Park.** Corcoran: housing runs from textbook mid-century Florida ranch to large lakeside estates, the latter split between century-old brick estates and architecturally significant modern homes; the most sought-after properties sit on a chain of lakes linked by canals or within walking distance of Park Avenue. The city is characterised by brick streets and live oak trees. Windsong was built 2001–2016, 2,755–5,196 sq ft, HOA roughly $235–262/month. *Two completely different jobs under one area name: pre-war estates with original millwork, brick, and detailed trim that take hand-work and time, versus 3,000–5,000 sq ft modern houses that are large but fast. Mature live-oak canopy over brick streets means constant leaf and organic litter tracked onto entries and porches — quote entry/lanai work rather than assuming it. Lakefront and canal-side homes mean docks, boats and outdoor-to-indoor traffic. Estimate Winter Park by house, never by area average.*

**Maitland.** Dommerich Estates dates to 1957 and has kept developing since, homes 1,422–5,178 sq ft, including custom mid-century homes (one listing cites a 1961 Paul Pizer design); the area has Winter Park Chain of Lakes access and lake-access lots. *Late-1950s and 1960s stock at a 3.6× size spread — original bathrooms and kitchens with aged tile and grout in some houses, gut-renovated interiors in others. Mid-century modern homes typically mean large single-pane glass expanses and low-slope details, so glass and interior sills are a bigger share of the work than square footage suggests. Lake access adds sand and wet-foot traffic at rear entries.*

**Altamonte Springs.** NeighborhoodScout: Spring Valley is mostly medium (3–4 bedroom) to small single-family homes plus apartment complexes, predominantly owner-occupied, with most residences built between 1970 and 1999 and some after 2000; vacancy 10.5%. Sanlando Springs is small-to-medium apartments and single-family homes, predominantly **renter**-occupied, also mostly 1970–1999 build. *A 1970s–1990s, non-HOA-dominated, mid-size housing base — the natural home of recurring maintenance cleans on 3-bed/2-bath houses rather than large-estate work. The renter-heavy Sanlando Springs profile points at turnover work (move-out/move-in) as a distinct demand stream. Fifty-year-old bathrooms mean grout, caulk lines and glass that respond to restorative deep cleans, and owners should be told the difference between "clean" and "re-grout."*

**Baldwin Park.** Homes.com and the Orange Observer: built from the early 2000s on the former Naval Training Center under new-urbanist principles; homes range from small condos to 7,000-sq-ft houses, with custom homes along New Broad Street and Meeting Place down to smaller cottages, plus townhomes, apartments and live/work units; vintage-revival styles (Colonial Revival, Craftsman, Victorian); HOA fees can exceed $1,000/month; walkable to the Village Center, Blue Jacket Park and Lake Baldwin. *Homes are only ~20–25 years old, so this is condition-maintenance work, not restoration. The critical operational fact is the built form: alley-loaded, rear-garage, zero-to-narrow-lot new urbanism plus a mixed-use core means parking a crew van is a real constraint — plan alley access and confirm where a vehicle can legally sit. The condo-to-7,000-sq-ft spread inside one small neighborhood makes flat per-area pricing impossible. High HOA dues signal residents already buy services and expect professional standards; town-home stair-and-multi-level layouts add time per square foot.*

**College Park.** MaxLife Realty and Ben Laube Homes: platted in the 1920s land boom, largely built out by 1940, housing stock is Craftsman bungalows, Mediterranean Revival cottages and modest single-storey homes on brick-lined streets; ZIP 32804; Homes.com notes a mix of modest bungalows and contemporary infill houses, several lakes including Lake Ivanhoe and Lake Adair, and Dubsdread Golf Course dating to the 1920s. VeryApt notes cottages and bungalows from the early 1900s standing next to new construction. *Genuinely old housing — 85 to 105 years. Expect original wood floors and painted woodwork, small rooms with lots of trim and door casing per square foot, and small original bathrooms; labour per square foot runs high and the crew needs product discipline for finished wood. Detailed millwork and built-ins make deep cleans and pre-listing cleans the strongest fit. Street parking on narrow brick streets close to downtown is the access constraint. Golf-course-adjacent and lakefront homes bring outdoor traffic to rear entries.*

**Lake Nona.** Tavistock/Jome: a 17-square-mile master-planned community adjoining Orlando International Airport, built by Toll Brothers, ICI Homes, Dream Finders, Pulte, Beazer and David Weekley; Homes.com describes VillageWalk at Lake Nona as **guard-gated** with conservation homesites and maintenance-free living, and Summerdale Park as two-storey new construction. *Newest stock in the portfolio — production-builder homes, mostly under ~20 years old, and much of it two-storey. Guard-gated entries mean the crew must be pre-registered by name, not just given a code; build that into scheduling. Conservation-backing lots put houses against undeveloped land, so rear sliders, screens and lanais collect more debris than interior-lot homes. Maintenance-free/HOA product means owners are already buying services. Two-storey plans change crew time: stairs, upstairs bathrooms, and high entry glass.*

**Hunter's Creek.** MaxLife Realty: a seven-village master-planned community in south Orlando (32837) developed from the late 1980s into the early 2000s around the Hunter's Creek Golf Course, with all of it under a single, actively managed HOA; the oldest sections are 35+ years old and are **concrete-block construction with typical Florida production-builder floor plans of that era, varying in state of renovation**; newer phases have more modern plans. neighborhoods.com: attached and single-family homes, 599–3,892 sq ft, seven parks. Residents are ~15 minutes from MCO, 20 from Disney, 25 from downtown. *A 35-year age spread inside one community: late-1980s houses with original-era kitchens and baths sit next to early-2000s product, so scope varies house to house even on the same route. The 599–3,892 sq ft range means condos/townhomes and large pool homes are both in play — price by unit type. A single strong HOA across all seven villages is a real advantage for route density: one area, many homes, short drive times between jobs, no separate gate systems to learn per pod. Proximity to MCO and the parks suggests short-term-rental and relocation turnover demand worth testing.*

**Dr. Phillips.** Market Connect Realty: unincorporated Orange County between Universal to the north and the Bay Hill golf enclaves to the south, oriented toward the attractions corridor rather than downtown; the housing reads in three registers — Bay Hill and Isleworth-adjacent estates, **mid-century ranch neighborhoods off Turkey Lake Road**, and newer builds on the Butler Chain lakefront; gated subdivisions are central to the market, with roughly eight gated communities. Corcoran: former orange groves converted to subdivisions as Orlando grew after 1971; many homes sit around lakes and the area borders several gated golf communities. Nicole Mickle notes guard-gated communities here. *Three price and labour tiers in one area. The mid-century ranches off Turkey Lake Road are ordinary recurring-clean houses; the Bay Hill and lakefront estates are large, often with pools, guest suites and extensive glass, and belong on estate pricing with larger crews. Gating is the dominant operational fact: gate codes, guard check-in and per-community vendor rules govern whether a crew arrives on time. Golf-course-frontage homes have turf and irrigation right at the patio door.*

**Windermere.** Florida Neighborhood Realty: the incorporated Town is barely ~2.2 square miles with roughly 3,400 residents, sitting on a peninsula bounded by Lake Butler, Lake Down and Lake Bessie within the 11-lake Butler Chain, while the larger 34786 area extends to Disney's eastern boundary; **most subdivisions — Isleworth, Keene's Pointe, Casabella, Bellaria, Summerport, Belmere, Windermere Trails — have active HOAs with separate dues, architectural review and gate access**; inside the Town, WastePro collects with everything at the curb by 7:00 a.m., while unincorporated 34786 homes are served by their subdivision's contracted hauler or Orange County. Homes.com: Colonial Revival, New Traditional and Contemporary homes in Lake Down Cove, Keene's Pointe, Lake Butler Sound and Waterstone on Lake Butler; townhomes and condos in Lake Burden and the Lakes of Windermere; private clubs include Isleworth Golf & Country Club and The Golden Bear Club at Keene's Pointe. *This is the most access-constrained area on the list. Gated and guard-gated entries with architectural-review-grade HOAs typically also vet vendors, so expect insurance documentation and pre-registration per community — not one credential for "Windermere." The Town/unincorporated split matters practically: trash handling differs by side of the line, which affects what a crew does with bagged waste, and the 7:00 a.m. curb rule inside the Town is a hard constraint on early arrivals. Housing is large, lakefront and club-adjacent, with docks and pools, so expect estate-scale scopes plus significant glass facing the water. Also note the mix: Lake Burden and Lakes of Windermere townhomes and condos are a completely different, smaller product in the same ZIP.*

**Winter Garden.** Nicole Mickle: 14 miles from downtown Orlando on the banks of Lake Apopka, with established neighborhoods of varied architecture alongside a large set of new-construction communities. Homes by Marco: Independence is gated, has 24/7 staffed resident centres and an on-site elementary school, sits near The Hamlin and the 429 Expressway, with a median around $530,000, and there are roughly 69 other Winter Garden subdivisions in a similar price band. The Real Estate Collection: Summerlake blends new construction with established homes; Independence and Orchard Hills draw families with young children. *Predominantly recent, HOA-governed, family-occupied production housing — the core of a recurring-clean book, with high household density per square mile of driving. Gated communities with staffed resident centres mean check-in procedures; 24/7 staffing is helpful for crews needing access. Homes with young children in them change the actual work: floors, high-touch surfaces and bathrooms dominate over detail dusting. The 429 gives fast access from the west side, which matters for route building.*

**Ocoee.** Florida Neighborhood Realty: Wesmere is a gated master-planned community built primarily between 1991 and the early 2000s by Calton Homes with Beazer and Arvida, wrapping several large fountain ponds, with nearly 100 waterfront homes across 16 cul-de-sacs; Forestbrooke is a gated neighborhood in north Ocoee built 2003–2012 by Meritage and D.R. Horton with a mandatory HOA. Realty in Orlando: Forest Lake Estates was built 2017–2020, 278 homesites, 1,532–4,182 sq ft, with an HOA. Market Connect listings show townhouses around 1,653 sq ft and single-family homes around 2,303 sq ft. *A layered west-side market: early-1990s, mid-2000s and late-2010s stock in adjacent gated pods, so the same route hits 30-year-old and 6-year-old houses. Typical sizes cluster in the 1,600–2,300 sq ft range, which makes standard-package recurring cleaning the right product. Pond-front and cul-de-sac homes mean irrigation overspray and water-adjacent outdoor living at the rear of the house. Mandatory-HOA gated pods again mean gate access is the scheduling risk, not drive time.*

**Apopka.** Market Connect Realty: the housing "runs from post-war ranches near the historic downtown to new-construction estates on former grove land off Kelly Park Road," cypress-shaded lakes anchor several of the older subdivisions, and the newest subdivisions lean into golf, gated pods and larger lot sizes than most of Central Florida still offers; Wekiva Springs, Sweetwater, Magnolia Park and Errol Estates are gated. Nextdoor: Rock Springs Estates is surrounded by nature including Wekiwa Springs State Park. Homes by Marco: Apopka has 143+ subdivisions in the $420–430K median band. *The widest age range on the list — roughly 1950s ranches near downtown through brand-new estates. Post-war ranches downtown are small, single-storey, often with original baths, and suit deep-clean and turnover work; the Kelly Park Road estates are new, large and on bigger lots, which suits premium recurring service. Cypress-shaded lake lots and homes backing state-park land mean heavy tree litter and organic debris right at the house, so entries, screens and lanais need to be priced in rather than treated as extras. Larger lots also mean longer driveways and more walking from the vehicle to the door — real minutes per job. Apopka is geographically spread out; build routes tightly or the drive time eats the margin.*

Read the vacancy and renter figures only as a hint that Altamonte Springs carries turnover/move-out demand. **I retrieved no income, poverty, flood or crime data, so I am asserting nothing about market viability.** If you need that judgement, it needs its own search pass.

suburbs.housingCharacter: Housing runs from post-war ranches near the historic downtown to new-construction estates on former grove land off Kelly Park Road; cypress-shaded lakes anchor several of the older subdivisions, and the newest subdivisions lean into golf, gated pods and larger lot sizes than most of Central Florida still offers. Wekiva Springs, Sweetwater, Magnolia Park and Errol Estates are gated.

conditions.condition: The widest age range on the list, roughly 1950s ranches near downtown through brand-new estates.
conditions.implication: Post-war ranches are small, single-storey and often have original baths, suiting deep-clean and turnover work, while the Kelly Park Road estates suit premium recurring service.

conditions.condition: Cypress-shaded lake lots and homes backing state-park land, including Rock Springs Estates surrounded by nature near Wekiwa Springs State Park.
conditions.implication: Heavy tree litter and organic debris right at the house means entries, screens and lanais need to be priced in rather than treated as extras.

conditions.condition: Larger lots with longer driveways.
conditions.implication: More walking from the vehicle to the door, which is real minutes per job.

conditions.condition: Apopka is geographically spread out, with 143+ subdivisions.
conditions.implication: Build routes tightly or the drive time eats the margin.
